stages.title: Senior-role positioning and evidence
stages.prerequisite: Use existing professional backend experience; identify unknowns with a short diagnostic.

topics.title: Verify your CV against real evidence
topics.concepts: Every CV statement must have an accurate source and a clear status: professional work, existing personal project, or planned work. Do not use unverified dates or invented metrics.
topics.exercise: Create a table with one row per CV claim: exact claim, employer/project, your contribution, proof/link, and fact to confirm. Correct the Chainomation date only after checking it.
topics.assessment: Can you point to evidence for this claim? What did you personally do? Which facts still need confirmation?
topics.pass: All dates and titles have been checked; every important claim has evidence; planned work is not described as completed; uncertain facts are flagged rather than guessed.
topics.defer: Optional tools and advanced variants not required by target roles; add only when job evidence or project needs justify them.

topics.title: Find and compare senior remote vacancies
topics.concepts: Remote does not always mean worldwide. Check location and contractor rules from the employer posting, compare role scope with your evidence, and record hours in UTC and Dhaka time.
topics.exercise: Compare 10–15 active senior vacancies. For each, record posting URL/date, Bangladesh eligibility source, responsibilities, required skills, three evidence matches and gaps. Save five qualified roles and apply to the two strongest matches.
topics.assessment: Why is each saved vacancy eligible and a fit? Which three requirements can you prove? What is your next action?
topics.pass: A role comparison is complete, five eligible roles are in the tracker, two tailored applications are submitted when suitable vacancies exist, and repeated gaps are prioritized.
topics.defer: Optional tools and advanced variants not required by target roles; add only when job evidence or project needs justify them.

topics.title: Turn real work into senior interview examples
topics.concepts: Senior interviews look for judgment and ownership: constraints, alternatives, decision, delivery, collaboration, outcome and learning. Be precise about your contribution versus the team's.
topics.exercise: Write three stories from completed ERP/CRM, inventory/accounting, insurance or AI-project work. Include a real artifact where possible, then record a concise 90-second answer for each.
topics.assessment: What was the problem and constraint? What did you own? What options did you consider? What evidence shows the result? What would you change?
topics.pass: Three truthful stories explain a decision and trade-off, distinguish personal/team contributions, cite evidence and fit a concise spoken answer.
topics.defer: Optional tools and advanced variants not required by target roles; add only when job evidence or project needs justify them.

topics.title: Prepare and send tailored applications
topics.concepts: Tailor the order and emphasis of accurate evidence to the role. Verify the posting, location, links, dates and overlap. Track the exact CV version and follow-up.
topics.exercise: Prepare senior .NET backend and AI integration CV summaries. Tailor them to real eligible postings, map three requirements to evidence, update profiles, and submit three to five well-matched applications if available.
topics.assessment: Does the application show proof for the vacancy's main requirements? Are all claims accurate and links working? Is the next action recorded?
topics.pass: The application pack is consistent, role-specific and truthful; each submitted application has proof links, a saved CV version and a follow-up date.
